newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel-Palestinian clashes not affecting shekel.
newsitem.headline: Israel-Palestinian clashes not affecting shekel.

text.p: Violent clashes between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers have not affected shekel trading, dealers said.
Although the dollar was rising against the shekel in morning trade, dealers attributed this to the U.S. currency's rise against the mark and not to the tense political situation.
Fifteen Palestinians have been shot dead in clashes with Israeli soldiers over the past two days, according to Palestinian health officials.
The dollar was trading at 3.1763 shekels against 3.1710 on Wednesday.
"The dollar-mark rate rose," a Bank Leumi dealer said. He noted that the basket of foreign currencies was little changed from Wednesday's representative rate of 3.5541 shekels.
He said that while there was slightly more interest in the dollar on Thursday, overall trade was very balanced.
"The basket is still seven percent below the slope," the dealer said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
